target_customer: Mobile app developers and publishers wanting deep links and monetization of in-app content
problem: Mobile apps were silos, so users could not link or move between content inside apps. URX built deep linking and then an ad product to connect users to relevant app actions.
business_model: Developer API and advertising (AppViews), revenue share with publishers
product_category: Mobile deep linking and app advertising

founders.name: John Milinovich
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO by YC blog and Fortune (2016).

founders.name: Nate Smith
founders.background_notes: YC page: designer and investor, later founder of Superoot (S18).

exit.reason: Acqui-hire of about half the team; Pinterest said it acquired no technology or assets and the AppViews ad product was shut down.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required indexing app content, a link resolution service and SDKs across iOS and Android before OS level deep linking standards existed.

defensibility.rationale: Platform owners controlled the standards, and rivals such as Branch and Button offered similar links.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google and Facebook launched app indexing and App Links; URX pivoted to ads then sold its team to Pinterest.

market_need_then: Mobile app usage was growing but links between apps were weak. Search and advertising firms were investing in this gap by 2014.

branding.domain_note: urx.com is now a parked page for sale (redirects to a domain marketplace).

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered products but no evidence of recognition beyond ad tech and developer circles.

pivots.why: Monetize deep links through ads; source for motive not found

outcome_analysis: URX raised 15M including a 12M Series A led by Accel at a reported 40M valuation in 2014 for deep linking. Platform owners absorbed the wedge, it moved into AppViews ads and in May 2016 Pinterest hired about half the team without buying the technology. The outcome was an acqui-hire after a raise at a higher valuation, not a venture return.
notes: Series A amount, date, valuation and investors cross-checked across the YC blog, TechCrunch and Business Wire snippets. Total raised was about 15M after the Series A, so about 3M came earlier, but no source itemizes the earlier round, so it is not recorded and funding coverage is partial. Founders: the YC page lists Nate Smith only; John Milinovich is named CEO by other sources. Education and prior employers not found. No competitors dated near 2013 found.
